title: Lumenary Chemistry
subtitle: Chemistry from a first look at atoms to the quantum chemistry, synthesis and AI-assisted discovery of 2026: matter and reactions, physical, quantum, organic, inorganic and analytical chemistry, and the chemistry of life and the planet.
description: Lumenary Chemistry is a subject of Lumenary Scientia, free and open source like the others. It starts with no experience at all — what matter is made of and what happens when it changes — and climbs through the mole and the chemical bond, thermodynamics, equilibrium and kinetics, quantum chemistry and spectroscopy, organic, inorganic and analytical chemistry, and the chemistry of life, the environment and energy, to the methods changing chemistry in 2026: machine learning, self-driving laboratories and quantum computation.

Every lesson teaches with ideas first and calculation second. Calculations and simulations — stoichiometry, equilibria, rate laws, molecular orbitals, spectra — are in Python with NumPy, and every block with a **Run in browser** button runs there, with nothing to install. A lesson says *Code tested* only when all of its code passed. Lumenary Chemistry links to [Lumenary Materials](/en/materials/) for solids and to [Lumenary Math](/en/math/) for the mathematics underneath.

Chemistry is practised safely or not at all. The only experiments these lessons suggest are kitchen-safe ones, done with an adult; everything else is for a properly equipped laboratory with trained supervision. The lessons never give instructions for making hazardous substances, and they teach how to read hazard labels and safety data sheets.

Every lesson was drafted with AI assistance and is awaiting review by a human chemist. The text, exercises and code are original and licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (code Apache-2.0). Where a laboratory, society or database has published the primary source — a paper, a data sheet, IUPAC's recommendations — the lesson links to it rather than retelling it.

levels.title: Matter and change
levels.summary: No experience needed, from about age 11. What matter is made of, how to work safely, atoms and the periodic table, molecules and compounds, chemical reactions, and acids and bases in everyday life.

levels.title: The language of chemistry
levels.summary: The ideas every chemist uses daily: atomic structure and the periodic table, the chemical bond, the mole and stoichiometry, gases, liquids and solids, and solutions.

levels.title: Physical chemistry
levels.summary: Why reactions go and how fast: thermochemistry, entropy and free energy, chemical equilibrium, acids, bases and buffers, kinetics, and electrochemistry.

levels.title: Quantum chemistry and spectroscopy
levels.summary: Where chemical behaviour comes from: quantum mechanics for chemists, molecular orbitals, spectroscopy, statistical thermodynamics, and computational chemistry.

levels.title: Organic chemistry
levels.summary: The chemistry of carbon: functional groups and naming, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms, carbonyl and aromatic chemistry, and how chemists plan a synthesis.

levels.title: Inorganic and analytical chemistry
levels.summary: Beyond carbon, and how chemists measure: coordination chemistry, the solid state and main-group elements, analytical chemistry, and catalysis and green chemistry.

levels.title: The chemistry of life and the planet
levels.summary: Chemistry at work in living things and in the world: biochemistry, medicinal chemistry, environmental and atmospheric chemistry, and the chemistry of energy.

levels.title: The frontier of chemistry
levels.summary: Where chemistry is moving in 2026, with links to the primary sources: machine learning for molecules and reactions, self-driving laboratories, quantum computing for chemistry, new reactions and framework materials, and sustainable chemistry.

references.title: IUPAC
references.note: The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry: nomenclature, symbols, units and the periodic table.

references.title: PubChem
references.note: A free database of chemical structures, properties, safety and toxicity data.

references.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook
references.note: Thermochemical, spectroscopic and physical data for thousands of compounds.

references.title: LibreTexts Chemistry
references.note: Free, openly licensed chemistry textbooks at every level.
